V2-01.question: For every unordered pair of distinct transacted products sharing a customer, compute customer-set Jaccard similarity. Return columns: product_a, product_b, shared_customers, union_customers, jaccard. Order: product_a, product_b ascending. Use distinct non-NULL CustomerID/ProductID edges, product_a < product_b; union is customers buying either product, intersection is customers buying both.

V2-02.question: Count equivalence classes of customers with identical nonempty purchased-product sets, by set size and class size. Return columns: product_count, customers_per_class, class_count. Order: product_count, customers_per_class ascending. Use distinct non-NULL customer-product edges. Product order is irrelevant. Include singleton classes.

V2-03.question: For each size of the smaller set, count ordered pairs of active stations where one purchased-product set is a proper subset of the other. Return columns: smaller_product_count, station_pair_count. Order: smaller_product_count ascending. Use distinct non-NULL station-product edges; A is a proper subset of B if all A products occur at B and B has more products. Count each ordered (A,B) once.

V2-04.question: For each unordered product pair bought by at least two common customers, compute customer-level co-purchase lift. Return columns: product_a, product_b, shared_customers, lift. Order: product_a, product_b ascending. Universe is distinct customers with any non-NULL product edge. Lift = shared_customers * universe_size / (buyers_of_a * buyers_of_b). Deduplicate repeated purchases.

V2-05.question: Summarize the customer-card graph by customer degree and card degree. Return columns: customer_card_degree, card_customer_degree, edge_count. Order: customer_card_degree, card_customer_degree ascending. Use distinct non-NULL (CustomerID,CardID) edges. Customer degree counts cards; card degree counts customers. Each edge contributes once.

V2-06.question: For each customer currency with known transaction Price, compute median Price and median absolute deviation from that median. Return columns: currency, observation_count, median_price, mad_price. Order: currency ascending. Join customers; exclude NULL currency/Price. Normalize Price before sorting. An even sample median averages the two middle values; MAD is the same median rule on absolute deviations.

V2-07.question: For each product with at least four valid unit-price observations, report Q1, Q3 and the strict Tukey-fence outlier count. Return columns: product_id, observation_count, q1, q3, outlier_count. Order: product_id ascending. Eligible rows have non-NULL ProductID/Price and Amount > 0. Unit price = normalized Price/Amount. Q1 and Q3 are nearest-rank values at ceil(n*0.25) and ceil(n*0.75). Outliers are strictly below Q1-1.5*(Q3-Q1) or above Q3+1.5*(Q3-Q1). Compare unrounded values.

V2-08.question: For each non-NULL ProductID with at least ten known Amount observations, compute its symmetric ten-percent trimmed mean Amount. Return columns: product_id, original_count, removed_each_tail, retained_count, trimmed_mean. Order: product_id ascending. Exclude rows with NULL ProductID or NULL Amount. Sort by Amount then TransactionID; remove floor(n/10) rows from each tail, preserving remaining multiplicity.

V2-09.question: For each product, list every modal known Amount and its frequency. Return columns: product_id, modal_amount, frequency. Order: product_id, modal_amount ascending. Exclude NULL ProductID/Amount. Mode means the largest frequency within product; keep all ties, not merely the largest Amount.

V2-10.question: For each currency, calculate the Gini coefficient of positive customer total Consumption in 2013. Return columns: currency, customer_count, gini. Order: currency ascending. Join monthly rows to customers with known currency; sum known normalized Consumption per customer in 2013, retain totals > 0. Sort total ascending with CustomerID tie-break. Gini = 2*sum(rank*total)/(n*sum(total))-(n+1)/n; one customer gives zero.

V2-11.question: For each currency, compute product quantity concentration using the Herfindahl index. Return columns: currency, product_count, hhi. Order: currency ascending. Use customer-joined transactions with non-NULL currency/ProductID and Amount > 0. Product shares use sums of Amount over that same cohort. HHI is sum of squared shares.

V2-12.question: For each currency, calculate the share of positive customer transaction-Price totals held by the top ten percent of customers. Return columns: currency, customer_count, selected_customers, top_share. Order: currency ascending. Sum known normalized Price per joined customer/currency; retain customer totals > 0. Select ceil(n*0.1) customers ordered by total descending, CustomerID ascending, with exact count (do not expand ties).

V2-14.question: For each station with identified product transactions, calculate Shannon entropy of its product mix. Return columns: station_id, transaction_count, product_count, entropy_nats. Order: station_id ascending. Use rows with non-NULL GasStationID/ProductID, count rows per product. Entropy = -sum(p*ln(p)), natural log, where p is product row share; one product gives zero.

V2-15.question: Compare CZE and SVK mean unit prices using a common product basket separately by customer currency. Return columns: currency, common_products, cze_index, svk_index, difference. Order: currency ascending. Join customers/stations, known currency/product, Amount > 0 and known Price. Retain products appearing in both countries within currency. Country-product mean is the unweighted mean of row unit prices; shared weights are pooled positive Amount per product across both countries, normalized across retained products. Difference = CZE index - SVK index.

V2-16.question: For every pair in the cross product of the observed non-NULL station-country and customer-currency domains, report observed transaction count and expected count under independence. Return columns: country, currency, observed_count, expected_count, pearson_component. Order: country, currency ascending. Use joined transactions with known country/currency. Include full cross product of observed country and currency domains, filling zero cells. Expected = country marginal * currency marginal / total. Pearson component = (observed-expected)^2/expected.

V2-17.question: Compute equal-segment standardized mean transaction Price by currency on segments present in every observed currency. Return columns: currency, common_segments, standardized_mean, raw_matched_mean. Order: currency ascending. Eligible joined rows have known currency/segment/Price. Common segments occur in every currency in that eligible universe. Standardized mean equally weights segment mean Prices; raw matched mean weights all eligible rows in the common segments.

V2-18.question: For each product, calculate population covariance between Amount and unit price. Return columns: product_id, observation_count, mean_amount, mean_unit_price, covariance. Order: product_id ascending. Use known product/Price and Amount > 0; unit price = normalized Price / Amount. Covariance = mean(Amount*unit_price)-mean(Amount)*mean(unit_price), population denominator n, unrounded intermediates.

V2-19.question: Reconcile observed transaction customer-month keys with monthly Consumption keys by coverage status. Return columns: coverage, key_count, transaction_count. Order: coverage ascending. Transaction keys require known CustomerID/Date, month formatted YYYYMM. Monthly keys must be valid YYYYMM. Classes both, monthly_only, transaction_only; include all classes with zero counts. Counts use full union of keys without fanout; transaction_count sums rows attached to keys in that class. Do not equate Price and Consumption.

V2-20.question: Count transactions by their complete dimension-reference quality signature. Return columns: customer_status, station_status, product_status, transaction_count. Order: customer_status, station_status, product_status ascending. Each reference status is NULL_KEY if FK is NULL, ORPHAN if non-NULL FK has no dimension row, otherwise MATCHED. Keep only observed signatures; each transaction appears once.

V2-21.question: Measure collisions when products are grouped by stored Description instead of ProductID. Return columns: product_ids_per_description, description_group_count, registered_product_count, transaction_count. Order: product_ids_per_description ascending. Exclude NULL Description; equality uses database collation. Include descriptions with no transactions. Group products by Description, then histogram by number of distinct ProductIDs per description; count transactions via ProductID without deduplication.

V2-22.question: For each customer segment and currency, census registered customers by presence in monthly and transaction facts. Return columns: segment, currency, monthly_present, transaction_present, customer_count. Order: segment, currency, monthly_present, transaction_present ascending. Include all registered customers, even absent from both facts; NULL segment/currency form groups. Presence is any row at any date, regardless of NULL measure; count each registered customer once.

V2-23.question: By currency, compare customer-product mean transaction Price to the same product’s peer mean after removing that customer. Return columns: currency, eligible_customer_product_pairs, above_peer_pairs, mean_price_gap. Order: currency ascending. Use customer-joined transactions with known currency/ProductID/Price. For each customer-product pair, own mean is its mean normalized Price. Peer mean uses all eligible transaction rows from OTHER customers of the same currency/product, weighted equally per row. Exclude pairs with no peer rows. Gap = own mean - peer mean; count strictly positive gaps before rounding. Average gaps equally across eligible customer-product pairs.

V2-45.question: Census sample customers by ProductID 2 purchase presence before and after the 2012-08-25 boundary, within currency. Return columns: currency, before_present, after_present, customer_count. Order: currency, before_present, after_present ascending. Universe is registered known-currency customers with any dated transaction in [2012-08-23,2012-08-27). Before window [2012-08-23,2012-08-25), after [2012-08-25,2012-08-27). Flags indicate at least one ProductID 2 transaction in each window, even when other products generated eligibility.
